major_concerns: Sourcing/constructing production-like, vendor-heterogeneous topologies from public data may not capture real vendor idiosyncrasies (limits external validity).
Deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish) may not model all vendor-specific behaviors → false positives/negatives in intent-satisfaction labels.
Preregistration must tightly specify retry policy, prompt variants, and exclusions to avoid post-hoc tuning.
Ethical/data-sensitivity risks when synthesizing configs from public corpora.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact public sources and synthesis procedure for production-like topologies; include provenance and filtering criteria.
Define verifier modelling assumptions per vendor and plan for false-positive/negative analysis (manual adjudication subset).
Preregister sample-size/power calculations, retry policy, seed management, and allowable prompt variants.
Add explicit data-sensitivity review and removal criteria to avoid releasing sensitive patterns.

major_concerns: High ethical risk: publishing realistic adaptive injection patterns can enable misuse if not carefully redacted.
Realism of adaptive injections created from public corpora may not reflect real-world attacker sophistication.
Defenses' operational utility trade-offs (false positives blocking benign retrievals) must be measured and reported.
required_design_repairs: Institute an explicit ethics and responsible-disclosure plan (red-team oversight) and predefine what attack details will be redacted in publication.
Preregister attacker sophistication tiers and ensure adaptive injections are synthetic, labeled, and non-operational when released.
Define benign-retrieval corpora and utility metrics to quantify false-positive harms of defenses.
Specify classifier training/validation data, and ensure defenses are evaluated on held-out benign samples.

major_concerns: Risk of inadvertently including sensitive or copyrighted configuration fragments in a public dataset.
Creating high-quality human reference configs and verifier-ground-truth is labor-intensive and may be under-resourced at proposed scale.
Verifier assumptions and modelling choices may limit downstream comparability if not fully documented.
required_design_repairs: Provide an explicit source list, license review, and filtering/PII-removal pipeline prior to release.
Define annotation protocol and human-validation steps for reference configs; allocate reviewer effort and QA checks.
Fully document verifier configuration, assumptions, and property encodings; include example scripts and adjudication policy for ambiguous cases.
Justify dataset size vs. annotation effort or adjust target accordingly; include distributional statistics in preregistration.

major_concerns: Mapping verifier feedback to structured repair prompts must be formalized; informal mappings risk irreproducibility and prompt-sensitivity.
Model-call cost accounting and latency/throughput trade-offs require precise preregistered budget and stopping rules.
Noisy or incomplete verifier modelling needs a defensible noise model and justification for experimental subgroup design.
required_design_repairs: Preregister exact repair-prompt templates, transformation rules from verifier output to prompts, and prompt-sensitivity probes.
Specify iteration budget (N), stopping criteria, and model-call accounting; include cost-normalized evaluation metrics.
Define verifier-noise injection procedure and rationale for the noisy-feedback subgroup; preregister sample sizes and analysis plan.
Include controls for regressions introduced by iterations and a manual-adjudication protocol for ambiguous regressions.
